summary: Iteration 3: targeted testing of the new features requested. Backend: 27 NEW pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py all pass, plus the existing regression suite (44 cases) — total 69 passed, 2 skipped (cookie-over-http env), 0 failed, run against the external preview host https://store-api-staging.preview.emergentagent.com (external /api/ now returns 200; probe fallback kept). Frontend: theme toggle works and persists on reload; anti-flash SSR class in index.html; /chat visitor invitation shown in French with login/register links; customer register → /chat → start conversation → send/send-disabled-on-whitespace verified end-to-end with real backend; admin login → /admin shows AdminPush panel (state='refusées' handled cleanly, denied-help visible, enable button disabled); /admin/messages lists conversations, admin reply sent successfully; /admin/commandes loads with no console errors; mobile viewport (390x844) shows bottom-nav with Chat entry, no horizontal overflow. Public /sw.js and /manifest.json served (200) with a push-only SW that navigates to /admin/commandes?order=<id> on notification click. No secrets appear in any response.

push.test_send_registered_endpoint_returns_41: PASS (transport-only assertion; real device delivery NOT exercised)
push.sw_notificationclick_targets_admin_comma: PASS by code review (pathname whitelist + query passthrough)

subscription_rule.existing_order_price_payment_creation_un: PASS (payments regression suite green, simulation mode)

push_transport_verification_scope: The pytest 'test send' hits real FCM through pywebpush and correctly receives a 4xx (endpoint token is bogus) OR a transport error — both branches are covered without ever returning 500 on our API. ACTUAL DEVICE/OS DELIVERY (browser -> FCM/APNs -> user device) was NOT exercised in this run because the Playwright browser context does not have a real user gesture and permission was 'refusées'. That path requires manual verification on a real device.
critical_code_review_comments: orders.py: subscription duplicate guard uses (a) a pre-insert find + (b) a Mongo partial unique index over pubg_id where items.type in [prime,prime_plus]. Concurrent-race test proves atomicity via the index. Good.
chat.py MessageIn uses ConfigDict(extra='forbid') which correctly rejects forged sender_id and other client-supplied fields. Good.
chat.py allowed_conversation() filters by user_id for non-admins, giving 404 rather than 403 so an attacker cannot even confirm a conversation exists. Good.
push.py validate_endpoint blocks non-https, non-standard ports, user:pass, query/fragment, and any host not in PUSH_ENDPOINT_HOSTS (fcm/mozilla/apple). Explicit SSRF hardening — good.

services/push.py never logs endpoint/token strings on failure (only exception class name). VAPID private key is loaded from env and never surfaced via /admin/push/config (only public key returned). Good.

public/sw.js is push-only (no fetch handler, no offline cache) so it can never interfere with API/payment traffic. notificationclick strictly whitelists pathname === '/admin/commandes' before opening, then passes query through — correctly navigates to /admin/commandes?order=<id>.
next-themes ThemeProvider uses storageKey='mgs-theme', defaultTheme='system', disableTransitionOnChange, attribute='class' — matches the SSR anti-flash class in index.html.
No new PAPI calls introduced; payments regression path stays in simulation mode (backend/.env PAYMENT_MODE=simulation) and all 8 payments tests pass unchanged.

MINOR: Duplicate-key error branch in orders.create_order compares keyPattern to {'pubg_id': 1} but the index name is 'one_subscription_order_per_pubg' and Mongo's keyPattern for a partial index is still {'pubg_id': 1}, so the equality holds. Confirmed by concurrent test producing exactly one 409.
